claimLedger.claim: Defines DRAM; common in pregnancy/after birth (up to 60%); seek women’s health physio; graded core work, posture and lifestyle advice; avoid early sit-ups/crunches/plank.
claimLedger.sourceSection: POGP · Tummy muscle separation (DRAM) in pregnancy · not stated
claimLedger.limitations: UK patient leaflet; symptom lists are not diagnostic criteria

claimLedger.claim: Separation usually returns toward normal by about 8 weeks; if still obvious then, contact GP for possible physio referral; avoid early sit-ups/planks/high-impact.
claimLedger.sourceSection: NHS · Your post-pregnancy body · not stated on fetched page
claimLedger.limitations: UK guidance; not a guarantee for every person; Indian follow-up timing may differ

claimLedger.claim: May improve on its own depending on severity and steps taken; never too late to work on with proper exercises; binders do not heal diastasis.
claimLedger.sourceSection: Cleveland Clinic · Diastasis Recti · Last updated on 04/21/2025
claimLedger.limitations: US patient education; uses finger/cm thresholds that should not become home diagnosis rules here
